questions.prompt: Which statement about the InfoNCE temperature tau is correct?
options: A smaller tau flattens the softmax, so all candidates become about equally likely.
Tau changes the number of negatives that the softmax is computed over.
A smaller tau sharpens the softmax, so hard negatives with high similarity are penalised more.
Tau matters only when the embeddings are not normalised to unit length.
questions.explanation: Logits are cos/tau: dividing by a small tau widens differences between candidates, so a hard negative close to the positive costs much more.

questions.prompt: InfoNCE with tau=1, positive cos 0.8, negatives with cos 0 and -1. Give the loss to 3 decimals.
One positive and 15 negatives, all cosines equal. What is the InfoNCE loss (3 decimals)?
A team reports 97% accuracy for a frozen probe, evaluated on a random 20% split of the same photo collection used for pretraining. What is the right reading?
questions.skillLabel: Evaluating an embedding with a probe
options: It shows the representation transfers to new cameras.
It is invalid because probes cannot be evaluated on held-out data.
It proves the encoder has no shortcuts.
It shows in-domain readability only; transfer needs a held-out domain.
questions.explanation: A random split shares the source's lighting, camera and backgrounds, so shift stays invisible.

questions.prompt: Cosine similarity of (1,1,0) and (0,1,1)? Give 2 decimals.
A frozen probe gets 0.88 in-domain and 0.55 on a shifted camera; the majority-class baseline is 0.50. By how many percentage points does the shifted result exceed the baseline?
questions.explanation: 55-50 = 5 points; most of the in-domain gain disappears (gap is 33 points).

questions.prompt: You have 50,000 labelled images from a domain similar to the pretraining domain. According to the standard guidance, what is reasonable?
options: Fine-tune the whole network at a small learning rate.
Train from scratch with a very large learning rate.
Only use a linear probe on the last layer.
questions.explanation: Large and similar data: fine-tune the whole network carefully.

rubric: Majority-class sets the floor for imbalanced labels.
An untrained encoder shows how much accuracy the probe and architecture give without pretraining.

questions.prompt: Six 2D points are embedded: class 0 = (1,0.2),(0.9,-0.1),(1.1,0.0); class 1 = (0.0,1.0),(0.1,1.2),(-0.1,0.9). A frozen nearest-mean (cosine) classifier is built from the class means of the unit-normalised points. All six points are then rotated by 60 degrees (counter-clockwise) and classified with those same means. How many of the six are classified correctly?
questions.explanation: The reference code reports accuracy 0.5 at 60 degrees, 3 of 6.
